q: Why did my sales drop yesterday?

checks.what: tool: measures the change with compare_period

answer:
Your premise is reversed: sales did not drop on 2026-10-13 — net sales rose from ₹40,119 on 2026-10-12 to ₹91,220 on 2026-10-13 (+127%). That means yesterday was better, not worse, versus the day before.

What changed (2026-10-12 → 2026-10-13)
- Orders rose 26.00 → 45.00 (+73.1%), driving most of the increase in net sales (orders × AOV). This is the largest volume change.
- Net AOV rose ₹1,543 → ₹2,027 (+31.3%), so each order brought more revenue as well.
- Ad spend increased ₹38,661 → ₹50,442 (+30.5%); sessions and ad spend moved together the same day (association found, not proven cause).
- Discounts widened ₹1,553 → ₹5,173 (added cost to net sales), and net sales deductions rose ₹5,110 → ₹6,569 — these trimmed part of the upside but did not reverse the gain.
- Return / cancel revenue fell (₹4,913 → ₹1,601) which also reduced gross-sales friction and supported net sales.

Confidence and interpretation
- The statistical check found no single causal driver meeting the threshold; several levers moved together (orders, AOV, ad spend). The overall change is within the normal historical range for net sales.
Worth checking: drill into which campaigns and products contributed the higher orders and AOV (the diagnosis flagged one ad and a few campaigns as unusual).
